content.thinking:
I'm laying out the order of the outcomes as decline, escalate, request docs, incomplete, then approve, with the order's SOP reference as 2.1. For unknowns I'm pulling the requirement from SOP 2.2, that a case with an unknown required fact can't be approved, and tying it to the incomplete outcome.

I'm working out who counts as an identified individual for the collections list: the control person and anyone owning 25% or more, based on the SOP's identification rules. I'm weighing whether anyone the agent listed but who falls below that threshold should be included, and whether certified ownership percentages change the 25% test.

I'm settling on who counts as an identified individual for the collections list: the control person and anyone owning 25% or more. I'm checking how the excluded-entity and nonprofit cases change that, since excluded entities skip beneficial owner and control person identification, while nonprofits only need a control person.

I'm questioning whether "identified individuals" means only those the agent listed, or those the SOP requires to be identified, meaning the control person and anyone at 25% or more. Excluded entities skip beneficial owner identification, so I'm checking how that changes who should be screened.

I'm settling on the gating: the control person counts, plus anyone at 25% or more, but only where the SOP actually requires identification. Excluded entities skip that step, so no one there is an identified individual, and nonprofits only add the control person.

I'm working out when the people list counts as empty: for excluded entities nobody needs to be identified, so an empty list is fine there. For non-excluded entities a control person is required, so an empty list isn't acceptable, and I'm checking how that interacts with the unknown handling.

I'm settling the excluded-owner sum: it only needs the owners who are excluded, so an entity with none still works out fine without a separate empty-list rule.

I'm checking whether the ownership completeness test needs anything beyond the unaccounted share: unaccounted_pct already leaves out excluded-entity shares, so if it reaches 25 or more the case goes to request docs. I'm also wondering whether an individual listed at 25% or more who isn't identified should trigger the same outcome.

I'm weighing whether an individual the agent didn't list but who owns 25% or more should count as an unidentified owner, since the SOP's completeness test is about unidentified people who could hold that share. The open question is whether that gap is a documents problem or an investigation problem, and I haven't settled which outcome it belongs under.

I'm checking whether an unlisted owner at 25% or more should count, since the SOP's identification duty applies to them too, and whether the 25% line is inclusive. I'm settling that the threshold is at least 25, so exactly 25% counts.

I'm checking whether the 10% held through an excluded entity should count as unaccounted, since its owners aren't traced. That would mean adding excluded shares under 25% to the open percentage, and I'm computing that total as a sum.

I'm checking whether a known person holding a smaller share could still reach 25% once the unaccounted percentage is added to their own share, since an unidentified owner might hold part of that gap.

I'm checking whether a person not counted as identified could still reach 25% once the open percentage is added to their own share. Since the rules only sum over counted people, I can't express that directly, and I'm weighing whether to widen who counts so the check covers them.

I'm weighing whether a person I haven't counted could still reach 25% once the unaccounted share is added to their known share, but the rules only add up over people already counted, so I can't express that check directly. I'm leaning toward keeping the test at open percentage 25 or more and not widening who counts.

I'm checking the rule for entities that are neither excluded nor nonprofit, where a control person has to be identified, and whether an all-excluded list changes that requirement.

I'm checking the remaining SOP rules: a non-excluded, non-nonprofit entity without a named control person gets request_docs, and any counted person whose identity isn't verified also means request_docs. I'm weighing whether the registry age under 12 months should trigger request_docs for every entity type. Finally I'm looking at the sanctions rule, where a confirmed entity or confirmed person hit leads to decline, and wondering whether to split it into two rules.

I'm checking the screening outcomes now: a potential sanctions match that hasn't been cleared means escalate, for the entity or any counted person. Any individual flagged as a PEP also leads to escalate. And adverse media on the entity or on any counted person calls for escalation too.

I'm checking the industry rules next: a prohibited industry means decline, and msb or crypto means escalate. I'm also looking at the licensed money services business exception that depends on its state license.

I'm checking the approval path next: the SOP has an escalate rule for msb and crypto, yet also says a licensed money services business with a verified state licence may be approved. As written, an approve rule for verified-licence msb would always lose to escalate under the order, so I'm weighing how to represent that conflict.

I'm settling on an approve rule with an empty all-condition, so it only applies when nothing above it fires, and I'm checking how unknown facts might still hold back that outcome.

I'm checking the approval path: the industry rule that escalates msb cases overrides the licensed-msb approve rule, so that approve rule can never win as written, and I'm leaving it as stated rather than adjusting the escalate rule. I'm also noting that the unlicensed money transmission wording needs to map onto the industry values.

I'm checking how a licensed money services business with an unverified licence fits the rules: "not verified" doesn't mean "unlicensed," so I won't treat it as prohibited. I'm also noticing that if the industry mapping has no entry for ordinary business types, those cases would come out unknown and push everything into incomplete, so I need to find out what industry values the case actually uses before settling the mapping.

I'm settling on a fixed list of common business words to treat as ordinary industries, since otherwise every normal case would come out unknown and fall into incomplete. That's a judgment call beyond what the SOP spells out, so I'll keep the list short and check it against the case's actual industry values.

I'm mapping the common business words to industry values, with cannabis and adult-content terms set to prohibited, crypto and virtual-currency terms set to crypto, and money transmission set to msb. I still need to decide whether ordinary industry words need mappings too, since otherwise normal cases would come out unknown.

I'm checking the sanctions rules: a sanctioned country on the entity or any counted person's residence leads to decline, and a high-risk jurisdiction leads to escalate, with IR, KP and SY in both lists where decline wins. I'm also noting that an unknown country could still make the decline rule possibly apply, which would push the case to incomplete.

I'm settling the citations for the collection rules: the counting rule draws on sections 3.1 through 3.3, and I'm checking the wording of the excluded-entity note so each cited section has a quoted sentence behind it.

I'm checking the wording of the collection rules now: the excluded-entity note, the control person requirement for other entities, and the 25% ownership test, so each cited section has a quoted sentence behind it.

I'm settling the ownership-completeness sum: it starts from the unaccounted percentage and adds the shares held by excluded owners that are under 25%, since their own owners aren't traced.

I'm settling the sum over excluded owners: an excluded entity holding under 25% still leaves its own owners untraced, so that share goes into the open percentage. For the incomplete-ownership rule, I'm drafting it as request_docs when the entity isn't excluded, isn't a nonprofit, and the computed open percentage is at least 25, with the SOP wording on complete ownership and requesting documents attached.

I'm checking which of the remaining needs are actual missing facts: whether adverse-media searches were recorded, which the SOP requires but gives no outcome for, and whether the unlisted partial owners can reach the 25% line once the unaccounted share is added.

I'm finishing the checks on the sanctions and identity rules, along with the verification requirement for identified individuals. I'm also noting that whether anyone outside the identified group could reach 25% once the unaccounted shares are added is still an open fact, since the rules only sum over counted people.

I'm checking the exact wording of the approve rule and the unknowns rule, quoting the section text as it appears, and deciding that the approve rule's catch-all will be written as an empty all-condition.

I'm writing out the counting condition for the collections list: a person counts if they're a control person of a non-excluded entity, or if they own at least 25% of a non-excluded, non-nonprofit entity. I'm also settling the section citations for the rules that have no outcome of their own.

I'm listing the remaining rule IDs for the ruleset: the approval catch-all, the missing control person case, ownership incomplete, unverified identity, stale registry, the sanctions and PEP checks, adverse media, the industry and geography rules, and the MSB licence approval. Next I'm lowercasing and trimming the map text so the entries match.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.unknown_when_empty: who the entity's control person and 25% owners are
people.text: Entities on the excluded list do not require beneficial owners to be identified. ... For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. ... Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies.

For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.
Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. The Approve item becomes the catch-all approve rule, which wins only when no other rule applies or might apply. The other items name the outcomes used by the later sections. 'Incomplete' is the outcome for unknowns.
Sets `order` (decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve).
Sets `unknowns`: a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete, which is section 1's outcome for a fact not yet established.

Excluded entities need no identified individuals. This is carried by people.counts_when (excluded entities have no identified individuals) and by people.empty_ok_when. It is also carried by the excluded = no conditions in cp-missing and ownership-incomplete.
Also part of people.counts_when: the control person of a non-excluded entity is an identified individual. The SOP's requirement of 'a single individual' is not checked separately.

Also part of people.counts_when: owners of 25% or more of a non-excluded, non-nonprofit entity are identified individuals. Computed open_ownership_pct adds two things: the unaccounted share, and shares held through excluded entities that hold less than 25%, since the pack does not trace owners behind an excluded entity. The SOP does not say what happens if the agent fails to list a known 25% owner. No rule was added for that; such owners count as identified individuals for 3.4 and section 4 regardless of `listed`.
The SOP does not say whose potential match counts. The rule applies to the entity and to identified individuals.

The materiality and source sentences define the bar, which the pack's adverse_media and entity_adverse_media facts already apply. The search-recording sentence has no outcome and no fact; see `needs`.
This contradicts 5.2. Every MSB is escalated under 5.2, and escalate outranks approve, so this rule can never decide a case. It is left as written for a person to resolve.
An individual's location is read as their residence.

needs.text: Record every search: the terms, the date and the sources reviewed.
needs.fact: Whether the adverse-media searches were recorded with their terms, date and sources. No given fact covers this, and the SOP gives no outcome when they were not recorded.

needs.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown.
needs.fact: Whether some named person below 25% could reach 25% if their known share_pct is added to the open share. Such a person is not an identified individual, so `some` over people cannot see them. A per-case fact or computed value (e.g. the largest unidentified person's share) would be needed to check this.

Such a person is not an identified individual, so `some` over people cannot see them. A per-case fact or computed value (e.g. the largest unidentified person's share) would be needed to check this.
